description: Fixed 30-message (30 user turns) dispatcher conversation for the HW6 Part 3 SHORT_TERM_N sweep. Facts the probes ask about are planted at turns 2, 3/20 (supervisor, later corrected), 9, 26 and 28 so that the different window sizes see different amounts of them.

planted_facts.2: name Dana Okafor, night-shift dispatcher at the Tamien depot
planted_facts.3: supervisor Marco Reyes (outdated - corrected at turn 20)
planted_facts.9: bus 4471 broke down at Santa Clara St & 5th St (overheating engine)
planted_facts.26: reports must be exactly three bullet points

messages: Good evening. I'm starting my shift on the incident desk tonight.
Quick intro so you know who you're working with: my name is Dana Okafor and I'm the night-shift dispatcher at the Tamien depot.
My shift supervisor tonight is Marco Reyes, so escalations go to him.
What categories do we use when logging incidents?
How should I decide between Delay and Service Change?
A rider just called about a light rail train running about 10 minutes late. Which category is that?
What details should a good incident description include?
How quickly should a breakdown be reported to maintenance?
Log this for me: bus 4471 broke down at Santa Clara St & 5th St at 9:40 pm with an overheating engine.
What should I tell riders waiting at that stop?
Is a replacement bus usually sent from the same depot?
What's the difference between an accident and a breakdown in our system?
A cyclist brushed a bus mirror on 1st Street, nobody was hurt. How do I categorize it?
Should minor collisions with no injuries still be reported to safety?
Give me a one-line template for logging a minor collision.
How do I mark an incident as resolved?
What counts as a service change versus a detour?
Line 68 is detouring around a water main break on Monterey Rd. How should I log that?
How long should a detour stay logged as open?
Correction to what I said earlier: Marco went home sick, so my supervisor for the rest of tonight is Lena Park.
Can you remind me what to check before closing an incident?
What does 'passengers affected' mean on the incident form?
Roughly how many passengers does a full articulated bus carry?
Is it better to log incidents immediately or batch them at the end of the shift?
What should I do if two riders report what seems to be the same incident?
Preference for the rest of the night: whenever I ask for a report, give it to me as exactly three bullet points.
What are common causes of delays on high-frequency routes?
Heads up: dispatch just reassigned me to cover Route 23 for the rest of my shift.
How do I escalate an incident that is getting worse?
Thanks, that's all the setup. I'll ask you a few check questions next.
